questions.question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of the high‑level overview shown in the system architecture chapter?

options.A: It lists every line of code that will be written.
options.B: It details the distribution of functions across system modules.
options.C: It provides a cost breakdown for each hardware component.
options.D: It defines the user interface color scheme.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] The chapter states that the high‑level overview “shows the distribution of functions across system modules” (Page 28).  

---

questions.question: According to the text, architectural components that are reused should be:

options.A: Designed only for a single specific project.
options.B: Kept hidden from other modules to avoid dependencies.
options.C: Shared across multiple system modules to promote efficiency.
options.D: Modified for each new requirement without documentation.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The passage notes that “architectural components that are reused should …” implying they are shared across modules (Page 28).  

---

questions.question: In the “Readers of different types of requirements specification” diagram, which stakeholder group is shown as a direct reader of system end‑users?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] The figure lists “System end‑users” as a separate reader category, indicating they read the requirements intended for them (Page 3).

questions.question: The feasibility‑study guidance states that if the answer to any key question is “no,” the project should:

options.D: Shift to a different development methodology.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The text explicitly says, “If the answer to any of these questions is no, you should probably not go ahead with the project” (Page 4).

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a system stakeholder for the Mentcare system?

options.B: Patients whose information is recorded in the system

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The stakeholder list includes “Patients whose information is recorded in the system” (Page 4).

questions.question: In the inspection and testing workflow diagram, which artifact is produced **immediately before** testing begins?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] The flow shows “System prototype” leading into “Testing” (Page 38).

questions.question: According to the testing figure, inspections are applied to which of the following artifacts?

options.A: Requirements, software, UML design, database schemas, program specification, architecture models

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The diagram lists inspections covering “Requirements, Software, UML design, Database … architecture models” (Page 38).

questions.question: When preparing a requirements document for an in‑house software product, which detail is most likely to be omitted?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] The text notes that an in‑house document “will leave out many of detailed chapters suggested above” and focus on user and high‑level nonfunctional requirements (Page 28).

questions.question: The purpose of showing the “distribution of functions across system modules” in the architecture overview is to:

options.A: Assign each developer a fixed salary.
options.B: Visualize how responsibilities are allocated among modules.
options.C: Determine the exact launch date of the product.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] The overview is described as displaying the “distribution of functions across system modules” (Page 28).  

---

questions.question: Reusing architectural components, as suggested in the text, primarily helps to:

options.A: Increase the number of unique bugs in each module.
options.B: Reduce development time and promote consistency.
options.C: Ensure each module is written in a different programming language.
options.D: Hide critical functionality from system architects.

questions.explanation: [Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The passage implies reuse of components is advantageous for efficiency, which aligns with reducing development time and maintaining consistency (Page 28).
